findings.title: group.users.delete(user_id) passes an integer ID instead of a record object
findings.body: ActiveRecord's CollectionProxy#delete expects model instances, not integer IDs. Passing `user_id` (an integer from `params.require(:user_id).to_i`) will not match any User record in the association, so the member will silently not be removed. The fix is to find the user first (e.g., `user = User.find(user_id)` then `group.users.delete(user)`) or use `group.user_ids -= [user_id]`.

findings.title: totalPages computed property over-counts by one when user_count is evenly divisible by limit
findings.body: The formula `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an incorrect result when user_count is an exact multiple of limit. For example, 50 users with limit 50 yields totalPages=2, but there is only 1 page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` instead.

findings.title: Each helper is never closed with {{/each}}
findings.body: The `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` block on line 21 is opened but never closed with `{{/each}}`. The next line (22) is the closing `` for the parent container. This will cause a Handlebars template compilation error or malformed DOM, preventing group members from rendering correctly.

findings.title: Unbounded limit parameter allows dumping entire user table
findings.body: The `limit` parameter from user input is used directly in the query with no upper bound. A malicious or careless client can pass an extremely large value (e.g., limit=999999999) to force the database to return and serialize all group members in a single response, causing memory pressure and slow responses. Cap the limit to a reasonable maximum (e.g., 1000).

findings.title: Test uses PUT but the route for remove_member is DELETE
findings.body: The test `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42` sends a PUT request, but the route is defined as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. While controller specs may bypass routing and call the action directly, this test does not verify that the correct HTTP method is enforced. It should use `xhr :delete` to match the route definition and catch potential routing misconfigurations.

findings.title: Missing semicolon after .then() in addMembers may cause ASI issues
findings.body: The `addMembers` method's promise chain ends with `})` on line 59 without a trailing semicolon. While JavaScript's automatic semicolon insertion usually handles this, it can cause subtle bugs if the next line in a minified or concatenated bundle begins with `(` or `[`.
